transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me today. Um, I guess I'm here because I've been having a little trouble with... well, with eating sometimes. It's probably not a huge deal compared to what you usually see, but... what really made me come in is that once I start eating like that, it's like, I don't know, it feels like I hit some switch. And I just keep going, even while part of me is thinking, Dennis, just stop already. 

It's really embarrassing to admit, honestly. Does that make sense? I just wanted to see if maybe you could help me figure it out, if that's okay.
Do you usually feel guilty or ashamed after one of these eating episodes?

Um, yeah... I do. It's, well, it's really embarrassing to talk about, honestly. I hope it doesn't sound too weird, but afterward, I just feel kind of... grossed out with myself? 

It's just hard because I’m usually pretty disciplined with things, like my college classes and my robotics team. I like to stay on top of all that and do a good job. So when I eat like that, it just makes me feel like I’m completely not in control of myself. I try not to make a huge deal out of it, but... yeah, it really bothers me. Is that... is that a normal way to react?
When you're eating like that, do you feel like you're unable to stop yourself?

Yeah, um... exactly. Like I was kind of saying earlier, it really does feel that way. It's not like I'm completely out of my mind or anything, I don't want to make it sound more dramatic than it actually is. But... yeah. 

Once I start, it's like my hands just won't listen to my brain. I'll be sitting there thinking, you know, *Dennis, just stop already*, but I just keep going anyway. It really is like a switch flips and I just can't make myself quit. I hope I'm explaining that okay... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you ever try to make up for these eating episodes by doing something to compensate, like exercising or vomiting?

Um, no, I don't really do anything like that. I mean, I try to stay somewhat active anyway, just for general health, but... no, I've never made myself throw up or anything extreme like that. 

I guess I just kind of sit with the feeling afterward. I try to just move on and tell myself I'll do better the next day. I hope that's the right way to handle it... or at least, not the worst way? I just try not to let it ruin everything else I have going on. Does that make sense?
How often do these episodes of eating like that happen?

Um, well, it's not like an every single day kind of thing. I really try to keep it under control. But... I guess since early in the semester, it's been happening most weeks. Usually just one night a week, maybe sometimes two if I have a lot of deadlines coming up or if there's just a bunch of food sitting around the apartment. 

It's been pretty much like that for, I don't know, maybe the last three or four months? I hope that doesn't sound too awful. I really am trying to manage it better, I promise. Is... is once or twice a week considered a lot?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?

Um, no, not really. I don't actually own a scale at my apartment or anything, but... my clothes all still fit exactly the same. So I haven't noticed any big jumps up or down. 

I really try to be careful so things don't get out of hand, you know? I'm guessing that's a good sign, right? Like, maybe it means I'm not doing too much damage overall with... with how I've been eating? I hope so, anyway.
Do you feel like you're in control of what or how much you're eating when these episodes happen?

Um... well, mostly I feel like I have a pretty good handle on things, you know? I try really hard to be disciplined. But... I guess during those specific times, maybe not as much. 

That's actually kind of the main reason I decided to come in. It's... it's a little embarrassing to admit, but once I start eating like that, it almost feels like I hit some kind of switch. I just keep going, even while part of me is sitting there thinking, Dennis, just stop already. 

I really do try to stop, I promise. It's just hard in that exact moment to actually do it. I know I should just be able to put the food away, and I really want to get better at that. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound completely crazy or anything... I'm usually much more put together than that, I swear.
Do you usually eat like that when you're feeling stressed or emotional?

Um, I'm not really sure? I don't think I'm a super emotional person, generally speaking. I try to keep a pretty positive attitude about things, you know? So I wouldn't say I'm eating like that because I'm sad or upset or anything. 

I know I mentioned deadlines before, but... I don't know if I actually feel super stressed when it happens. It just sort of... happens. I haven't really noticed a specific feeling that sets it off, to be honest. 

I hope that's an okay answer? Like, is it normal if it's not really tied to being emotional? I just don't want you to think I'm not handling my classes or my life well. I'm actually doing pretty good in school, I promise.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time without feeling like you've lost control?

Um... no, not really. I mean, if I'm eating a lot at once, it's pretty much always when I get that... that feeling like I can't stop. 

When I'm just eating normally, like hanging out with friends or grabbing dinner, I'm totally fine. I can just eat a normal amount and be done, like anyone else. I don't really overeat unless it's one of those specific times I told you about. 

I'm really trying to make sure those times don't happen, though. I guess it's a good thing that I'm in control the rest of the time, right? Like, it means it's not an all-the-time problem? I hope that's how it works, anyway.
Do you often feel anxious or self-critical after these episodes of eating?

Um... yeah, I guess I do. It's... well, it's not a great feeling. 

After it happens, I just feel really embarrassed. And, um, kind of grossed out with myself, if I'm being completely honest. Which I know sounds bad. It's just... I'm usually so disciplined with everything else, you know? Like with my classes and my robotics team, I'm always on top of things. So when I do this, it makes me feel like I'm totally failing at being in control of myself. 

But I'm really working on it! I don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself. I know I just need to try harder to be disciplined in that area too. Is it... is it pretty common to feel that way after? I just hope you don't think less of me for it. I really am a responsible person most of the time.
Do you usually feel like you're eating really quickly during those episodes?

Um, yeah, I guess I do eat pretty fast when it happens. But it's usually because I'm just, you know, trying to multitask? 

Like, I'll be standing at my desk, trying to get some homework done before I jump into a game with my friends, and I'm just eating while I do that. So I'm not really paying attention to the food or tasting it much. And then, before I know it, it's just... gone. Like, in just a few minutes. 

I know it sounds bad to eat that fast, but it's really just because I'm trying to be efficient with my time, you know? Like, I don't want to fall behind on my work. That makes sense, right? Like, a lot of college students probably eat pretty fast when they're busy? I just want to make sure I'm not doing something completely weird.
Do you usually eat like that when you're alone or do you try to hide it from others?

Um... well, I guess I do prefer to be by myself. It's not that I'm trying to be sneaky or anything! It's just... I don't know, I guess I'd feel a little self-conscious. 

Like, if my roommates are hanging out in the kitchen or whatever, I'll just grab a normal-ish amount of food, you know? Just like a regular snack or a normal plate so I fit in. But then... well, sometimes I'll kind of take some extra stuff back to my room with me later. Just because I don't really want them to see how much I'm actually eating. 

I just wouldn't want them to think I'm being weird or unhealthy. That's pretty normal, right? Like, wanting a little privacy when you're just kind of snacking a lot? I just don't want to make anyone else uncomfortable.
Do you usually feel uncomfortably full after one of these eating episodes?

Um... yeah, I guess I do get pretty full. But I think that's just because I'm not really paying attention, like I said before. 

It's not like I'm trying to stuff myself or anything! It's just... well, I usually only stop when my stomach starts feeling kind of tight and heavy. Like, to the point where it's actually a little uncomfortable to keep sitting at my desk, and I feel like I need to just go lie down on my bed for a bit. 

I know that probably sounds like I'm eating way too much, but I think it's just because I'm so focused on my games or my homework that I don't realize I'm full until it's a little too late. That happens to a lot of people when they're distracted, right? I'm definitely going to try to be more mindful about it so I don't get to that point anymore. I just hope it doesn't make me sound like I have zero self-control.
Have you ever had a period where you lost a significant amount of weight, only to gain it back?

Um, no, not really. My weight has stayed pretty much the same for a while now. 

I mean, maybe it fluctuates by a couple of pounds here and there depending on finals week or how stressed I am, but nothing major. I try to keep it pretty steady, you know? Like, I've never done any of those extreme diets or anything where I drop a ton of weight and then gain it all back. 

That doesn't sound very healthy, right? I just try to be pretty normal about that kind of stuff, I guess. So, yeah, no big changes or anything like that. That's a good thing, right?
Do you often feel like you're a failure after these eating episodes?

Um... I wouldn't say "failure," exactly. That's a pretty strong word, you know? But... well, yeah, I guess I do feel a little embarrassed afterward. And maybe kind of... grossed out with myself? 

It's just that I'm usually really put together. Like, I'm super disciplined when it comes to my classes and my robotics team, so... I don't know, doing this just makes me feel like I'm not in control, and I hate feeling like that. It's just a little out of character for me, I think. 

But it's not like I'm sitting around hating myself or anything! It's just a temporary thing, you know? Like, I just get a little frustrated and then I try to move on and do better the next day. That makes sense, right? Everyone gets a little down on themselves sometimes when they slip up.
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short period of time without feeling guilty afterward?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I think I almost always feel at least a little bit bad after I do it. 

It's not like a crushing, terrible guilt every single time, but... I definitely don't feel great about it. Like I said, it just feels like I slipped up, and I get annoyed with myself for letting it happen. I try to brush it off and tell myself it's fine, but the guilt is usually there in the back of my mind. 

I guess that means I care, right? Like, it would probably be worse if I just ate all that and didn't feel anything at all. That would mean I've totally given up, and I definitely haven't done that! So, yeah, I'd say the guilt is pretty much always there, even if it's just a little bit. That's a normal reaction, don't you think?
Do you think these episodes of eating happen more often when you're under a lot of stress?

Um, yeah, I guess you could say that. Stress definitely plays a big part in it. 

Like, since early in the semester... I'd say for at least the last three or four months, it’s been happening most weeks. But usually it's just one night! Sometimes two, if I have a ton of deadlines hitting all at once, or, you know, if there's just a bunch of extra food piled up in the apartment that my roommates bought. 

But it's been a pretty steady pattern like that. It's not an every-night kind of thing at all. I mean, college is stressful, so I feel like a lot of guys probably do the exact same thing when they're studying late or feeling the pressure. It's just a normal way to cope with being a student, right? I'm sure you hear that all the time from people my age, don't you?
Do you think the episodes of eating happen more often when you have upcoming deadlines or exams?

Yeah, definitely. I actually think I just mentioned that, but yeah, exams and deadlines are a huge trigger for me. 

Like I was saying, it's been happening most weeks since early in the semester, so probably the last three or four months? But usually, it really is just one night a week. Two nights at the absolute most, if I have a ton of midterms or project deadlines all hitting at once. Or, you know, if my roommates happen to buy a bunch of extra snacks and leave them around the apartment. 

But I try really hard to keep it under control so it doesn't get worse than that. One or two nights a week when things get crazy... that's not too extreme, right? I feel like a lot of college guys probably do the exact same thing when they're cramming. You probably see a lot of students who get a little off track during finals, don't you?
Do you think these episodes of eating happen more often when you're feeling emotional, like anxious or upset?

Um, not really? I don't think I get super emotional or upset very often, to be honest. I try to keep a pretty level head about things. 

Like I was saying, it's mostly just the pressure from school and exams. If I'm anxious about a specific test, then maybe, but not like... deep emotional stuff, if that makes sense? I think I handle my actual emotions pretty well. I'm definitely not doing it because I'm sad or crying or anything like that. 

It really is just the normal college stress getting to me every now and then. That's a lot better than it being a heavy emotional issue, right? I feel like just being stressed about school is a pretty normal reason to overeat a little bit, don't you think?
